messages:
alex: Quick sync — I dropped a short PRD draft in Drive for the Launch Gates + Pinning work. Need product + eng alignment on prioritization, acceptance criteria, and rollback rules before we hand this to eng. Link: https://go.redwood/pgd-launch-gates :spiral_note_pad:

maria: Thanks. Can you call out the customer-driven asks we promised in Q2? I want those prioritized if they affect SLA or pinning behavior.

ajex: typo — meant alex :)

alex: oops — fixed. Main asks: (1) Tenant-level version pinning for regulated customers, (2) soft-pinning for experiments to reduce noisy rollbacks, (3) admin UI to view pin TTLs and pending rollbacks.

tj: For acceptance criteria, suggest: measurable latency and correctness gates + experiment risk budget. Example: canary must show <5% increase in 95th latency and no more than 0.5% degradation on eval prompt set.

sara: +1 to concrete numbers. Also add an error-rate SLA: request error rate <0.1% at 99th percentile. If breached for 10m, trigger auto-rollback.

ben: On scope negotiation: do we ship tenant-pin API first (simple pin/unpin + TTL) and then adaptive pinning later? That would reduce scope and unblock customers.

alex: That's the proposed phased plan in the doc: Phase 1 = deterministic pin API + admin visibility; Phase 2 = adaptive pining (traffic-aware) + UI for experiments. Need eng sign-off on rollout/rollback automation.

oliver: From eng side — main risk is cache invalidation and KV state when switching models at runtime. We'll need a migration plan for long-lived sessions. Also need per-tenant KV eviction TTLs.

maria: Can we include an explicit edge-case about mixed-session pins? e.g., tenant pins v1 but some sessions pinned v2 by older clients. Acceptance criteria should include deterministic session routing and documented behavior.

tj: Drafting short rollback rules here: 
```
- Auto-rollback triggers: error_rate > 0.1% for 10m OR 95p latency regression > 5% for 10m OR quality regression on eval set > 1% absolute drop
- Manual rollback: owner can rollback via API and console. Rollback must preserve in-flight sessions for <30s before switching fallback.
- Soft-pin expiry: default TTL = 24h; admins can extend to 7d.
```

sara: For A/B experiment design: Hypothesis: adaptive pinning reduces cost by 12% without affecting quality. Metrics: per-token cost, 95p latency, eval-accuracy. Experiment buckets: 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with hold windows (2h, 6h, 24h).

ben: Important to call out model compatibility fallback: if target variant not available, route to last-stable variant and annotate trace with fallback_reason. Gate: if fallback rate > 2% for 30m, pause rollout.

alex: Good. One more product tradeoff: strict pinning guarantees deterministic outputs but increases capacity fragmentation. Adaptive pin reduces fragmentation but adds non-determinism. We should let customers opt-in per-tenant.

oliver: Engineering ask: need an ops playbook for emergency rollback that includes capacity pre-warm steps and KV priming commands. I'll add a short runbook and attach to the PRD.

maria: Prioritization ask: which customers require tenant-pin GA before Q2? I can create a short list and reach out. If we have >3 enterprise requests, move the deterministic pin earlier.

alex: I'll surface customer list and update PRD with clear launch gates: product sign-off, eng sign-off on rollbacks + runbook, QA regression pass on eval set, and monitoring hooks deployed (latency, error, fallback rate).

rollout-bot: scheduled canary job created for 1768509000 (canary id: cg-472). Notified: eng-oncall.

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll update the PRD with the gates and ping again for a quick review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
